mainTopic: Babies who become fit for מילה between the slaughter and the eating of the פסח; an ערל receiving הזאה; and the מצוה of פריעה
overview: This amud continues the search for a baby boy who is not yet fit for מילה when the קרבן פסח is slaughtered but becomes fit by the time it is eaten. A baby who recovers from illness waits seven full 24-hour periods (מעת לעת), so his wait can end in the middle of the day. A teaching from the sage of לוד seems to say otherwise, but the גמרא explains that the healing day is stricter than the birth day. רב פפא, רבא, רב כהנא and רב שרביא each give another case: a sore eye that heals, parents freed from prison, a טומטום found to be a boy, and a baby whose head came out before the rest of his body. The גמרא defends רב שרביא's case: either the mother's fever kept the baby alive, or a crying baby can live. Next, רבי יוחנן rules that an ערל can be purified by הזאה, and proves it from the Jews in יהושע's time, who were sprinkled before their מילה and brought the פסח in טהרה. רב then teaches that פריעה was not given to אברהם, learning it from the words ״שוב״ and ״שנית״ in יהושע. The amud ends by asking why the Jews did not do מילה in the מדבר; one answer is the weakness from the journey, and the second answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Recovery days are counted as full 24-hour periods
steps.stepSummary: The ruling ends: the seven recovery days for a sick baby must be full 24-hour periods (מעת לעת).
steps.simpleTranslation: From time to time, meaning full 24-hour periods.
steps.whatsHappening: These two words finish a ruling that began before this section: after a baby recovers, the seven waiting days before his מילה are counted as full 24-hour periods. The next step will challenge this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the baby got better in the afternoon, we wait until that same afternoon hour seven days later. Because the count ends at an exact hour and not at the start of a day, the seven days can finish in the middle of the day. That is how a recovered baby can become fit after the פסח is slaughtered but before it is eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: From time to time; a full 24-hour period counted from a set hour to the same hour

phrases.english: From time to time.
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from just before: each of the seven recovery days has to be a full 24 hours.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ruling about a recovered baby's waiting period that started before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A baby who recovered from illness waits seven full 24-hour periods before מילה.

steps.title: Challenge from the teaching of the sage from לוד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the 24-hour rule. The sage from לוד taught that the healing day is like the birth day, and a birth day does not need 24-hour counting.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the sage from לוד taught: the day of his healing is like the day of his birth. Doesn't that mean: just as for the day of his birth we don't need full 24-hour periods, so too for the day of his healing we don't need full 24-hour periods?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching that seems to contradict the rule just stated. If healing is compared to birth, maybe partial days should count after healing too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A baby born in the afternoon is circumcised at the very start of the eighth day, without waiting until the same afternoon hour. The challenger reads the comparison as meaning the healing count works the same way, which would cancel the מעת לעת rule.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't someone teach? (opens a challenge from a teaching)
The sage from the city of לוד
Doesn't it mean...? (suggests a reading of a source)

phrases.english: But the sage from לוד taught:
The day of his healing is like the day of his birth.
Doesn't that mean:

phrases.aramaic: מָה יוֹם הִוָּלְדוֹ לָא בָּעֵינַן מֵעֵת לְעֵת,
phrases.english: Just as for the day of his birth we don't need from time to time,

phrases.aramaic: אַף יוֹם הַבְרָאָתוֹ לָא בָּעֵינַן מֵעֵת לְעֵת?
phrases.english: So too for the day of his healing we don't need from time to time?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the מעת לעת rule from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that recovery days must be full 24-hour periods.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The sage from לוד compared the healing day to the birth day. Since the birth count does not need 24-hour periods, the healing count should not need them either.

steps.title: The healing day is stricter than the birth day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the challenge. The sage from לוד meant that the healing day is even stricter than the birth day, and it does need full 24-hour periods.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the day of his healing is stronger than the day of his birth. For the day of his birth we don't need full 24-hour periods, but for the day of his healing we do need full 24-hour periods.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the comparison was misread. The healing day is not equal to the birth day; it is stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'like the day of his birth' do not mean 'counted the same way.' The healing day is considered more weighty, so it needs a full 24-hour count, while the birth day does not. The מעת לעת rule from step 1 stands.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'עדיף' as 'better' in the sense of easier. Here the healing day is 'stronger' because it needs MORE waiting: full 24-hour periods.
steps.whatToRemember: A recovered baby waits seven full 24-hour periods (מעת לעת) before his ברית. A newborn may be circumcised as soon as the eighth day begins.

phrases.aramaic: לָא, עֲדִיף יוֹם הַבְרָאָתוֹ מִיּוֹם הִוָּלְדוֹ.
phrases.english: No, the day of his healing is stronger than the day of his birth.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִילּוּ יוֹם הִוָּלְדוֹ לָא בָּעֵינַן מֵעֵת לְעֵת,
phrases.english: For whereas the day of his birth does not need from time to time,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִילּוּ יוֹם הַבְרָאָתוֹ בָּעֵינַן מֵעֵת לְעֵת.
phrases.english: the day of his healing does need from time to time.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, עֲדִיף יוֹם הַבְרָאָתוֹ מִיּוֹם הִוָּלְדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2 by rereading the teaching of the sage from לוד.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the source: the comparison means the healing day is stricter, not identical.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Like the day of his birth' means the healing count works just like the birth count, with no 24-hour requirement.
steps.terutzMaskana: The healing day is stricter than the birth day and needs full 24-hour periods, so the מעת לעת rule stands.

steps.title: רב פפא's case: a baby with a sore eye
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives another case of a baby who is unfit when the קרבן פסח is slaughtered but fit when it is eaten: his eye hurt and he got better in between.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: For example, the baby's eye hurt him, and he got better in between.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא offers a different answer to the earlier question about how a baby could be unfit at the slaughter but fit at the eating. A baby with a sore eye can have his ברית as soon as he gets better.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier case used a sick baby whose seven-day recovery, counted מעת לעת, ended between the slaughter and the eating. רב פפא gives a simpler case. With a small problem like eye pain, the ברית waits only until the pain goes away, with no seven days. So the baby can recover and become fit between the slaughter and the eating.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the difference between a serious illness, which needs seven days of recovery, and a minor problem, where the ברית is done as soon as the baby is well.

phrases.english: רב פפא said:
For example, where the baby's eye hurt him
and he got better in between.
phrases.notes: In between means after the קרבן פסח was slaughtered but before it was eaten.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: כְּגוֹן דְּכָאֵיב לֵיהּ עֵינֵיהּ לְיָנוֹקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the מעת לעת discussion and returns to the larger question with a new example case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A new case that avoids the seven-day recovery problem.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The only case offered so far is a sick baby whose seven 24-hour recovery days ended between the slaughter and the eating.
steps.terutzMaskana: With a minor problem like eye pain, the baby can have his ברית as soon as he recovers, even between the slaughter and the eating.

steps.title: רבא: The Parents Were in Prison
steps.stepSummary: רבא's case: the baby's father and mother were locked in prison, and they were set free between the slaughter of the פסח and the eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: For example, where the baby's father and mother were locked up in prison.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own example of a baby who could not be circumcised when the פסח was slaughtered but had to be circumcised by eating time. The parents were in prison, so they could not do the מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the parents are locked up, nobody can circumcise the baby, so his not being circumcised does not block the father's פסח at slaughter time. Once they are freed before the eating, the מילה can be done, so the father may not eat until his son is circumcised. Here the baby himself is healthy and ready the whole time. Only the parents' situation changes.

phrases.english: Rava said:
For example, where his father and mother were
locked up in prison.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different case from רב פפא's. Here the change comes from the parents' situation, not the baby's health.
steps.terutzMaskana: A case where the parents were in prison during the slaughter and freed before the eating works.

steps.title: רב כהנא: A טומטום Found to Be a Boy
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא בריה דרב נחמיה's case: a טומטום was opened in between the slaughter and the eating and found to be a boy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא בריה דרב נחמיה said: For example, a טומטום who was torn open and was found to be a boy in between the slaughter and the eating.
steps.whatsHappening: A third אמורא gives his own example. At first nobody knew if the baby was a boy, so there was no מילה obligation. Then he was opened and found to be a boy, so the obligation started.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the פסח was slaughtered, the baby was a טומטום, so nobody could know whether he needed מילה at all. In between slaughter and eating it became clear he was male, so now he needs מילה. The change here is in what we know about the baby, not in his health.

keyTerms.meaning: A baby whose private parts are covered, so we cannot tell if it is a boy or a girl
In between, during the time between the slaughter and the eating

phrases.aramaic: רַב כָּהֲנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נְחֶמְיָה אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Kahana son of Rav Nechemya said:
For example, a tumtum who was torn open,
and was found to be a male in between.
phrases.notes: "In between" means after the פסח was slaughtered but before it was eaten.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב כָּהֲנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נְחֶמְיָה אָמַר: כְּגוֹן טוּמְטוּם שֶׁנִּקְרַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another separate example, parallel to רב פפא and רבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: A טומטום who turns out to be a boy between slaughter and eating works as a case.

steps.title: רב שרביא: Only the Head Came Out
steps.stepSummary: רב שרביא's case: the baby had pushed only his head out of the birth passage, and the rest of him came out later.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שרביא said: For example, where the baby pushed his head out beyond the corridor of the womb.
steps.whatsHappening: A fourth אמורא gives an example. The baby's head came out first, and his full birth was finished only later, between the slaughter and the eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the head comes out, the baby counts as born, so his eighth day is counted from then. But he cannot actually be circumcised until his whole body is out. If the rest of the body came out between slaughter and eating, the מילה became possible right then.

keyTerms.meaning: Corridor, the passage leading out of the mother's womb

phrases.english: Rav Sherevya said:
For example, where he put out his head
outside the corridor.
phrases.notes: The "corridor" is the birth passage. Only the head is out; the rest of the body is still inside.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁרֵבְיָא אָמַר: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהוֹצִיא רֹאשׁוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another separate example. This one is about a birth that happens in stages.
steps.terutzMaskana: A baby whose head came out first and whose body came out later can be the case.

steps.title: Can Such a Baby Even Stay Alive?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב שרביא with a ברייתא: once a baby comes into the air, his body switches how it lives. Otherwise he could not survive even an hour.
steps.simpleTranslation: But can such a baby live? Wasn't it taught in a ברייתא: once a baby comes out into the air of the world, what was closed opens and what was open closes, because if not, he could not live even one hour!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב שרביא's case. It argues that a baby with only his head out could not survive that long.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that when a baby reaches the outside air, the mouth and nose open and the belly-cord closes. A baby with only his head out has lost the cord's feeding but cannot eat yet. So he could not stay alive for the seven days that רב שרביא's case needs.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא? A strong challenge from an earlier source
The air of the world, meaning outside the womb
If not, were it not so

steps.confusionAlert: This challenge is only against רב שרביא's case. The cases of רבא and רב כהנא are not being questioned here.

phrases.english: But can he live?
But wasn't it taught:
Once he comes out into the air of the world,
the closed opens and the open closes.
phrases.notes: The mouth and nose open up, and the belly-cord that fed him in the womb shuts.

phrases.english: For if this were not so,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין יָכוֹל לִחְיוֹת אֲפִילּוּ שָׁעָה אַחַת!
phrases.english: he could not live even one hour!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly attacks the case רב שרביא just gave.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שרביא's case of a baby whose head came out seven days earlier.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says that once a baby is in the air, the feeding cord closes. Without eating he would die within an hour, so a baby with only his head out could not last seven days.

steps.title: A fever kept the half-born baby alive
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the ברייתא's challenge to רב שרביא: the baby with only his head out survived because a fever sustained him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we are dealing with a case where a fever kept him alive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב שרביא. The baby could survive with only his head out because the heat of a fever kept him going.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said a baby partly out in the air cannot live even an hour. The גמרא says that is the normal rule, but here there was an unusual situation: a fever sustained him. That lets the delay between the head and the body coming out still work for רב שרביא's case.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, what case are we dealing with? This phrase introduces a narrower case to answer a question.

phrases.english: Here, with what are we dealing?
For example, where a fever sustained him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's challenge from Step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to unusual circumstances
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A baby with only his head out cannot survive long enough for רב שרביא's case.
steps.terutzMaskana: A fever can keep such a baby alive, so the case is possible.

steps.title: Whose fever was it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose fever kept the baby alive. It rejects the idea that it was the baby's own fever, because then he would need seven days before his ברית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose fever? If you say his own fever, then if so, he would need a full seven days!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks the answer it just gave by asking whose fever this was. It shows that it can't be the baby's own fever.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the baby himself had a fever, he was a sick baby. A sick baby must wait seven full days after he gets better before his ברית. Then he could not be ready to be circumcised by the time the פסח is eaten, and the case of רב שרביא would fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces an option that will be rejected)

phrases.english: Whose fever?
If we say his own fever,
if so, he needs a full seven days!
phrases.notes: A baby who was sick waits seven days after he recovers before his ברית, so he would not be ready by the evening.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for details about the fever answer from Step 9
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whose fever sustained the baby: his own, or someone else's?

steps.title: It was the mother's fever
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the mother's fever kept the baby alive, so the baby himself was healthy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, his mother's fever sustained him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The fever was the mother's, not the baby's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The baby himself was never sick, so there is no seven-day wait. The heat from the mother's fever kept him alive while only his head was out. Once the rest of him came out, he could be circumcised right away.

phrases.english: Rather, his mother's fever sustained him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It was the mother's fever, so the baby was healthy and needs no seven-day wait.

steps.title: Second answer: a crying baby can live
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives another answer. The ברייתא's rule applies only to a baby who does not cry out. A baby who cries can live.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: this applies where he does not cry, but where he cries, he does live.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second, different way to defend רב שרביא from the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of needing a fever, this answer limits the ברייתא itself. Its rule that the baby can't survive an hour is only for a baby who is silent. If he cries, he is already breathing, so he can live with only his head out.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (introduces another answer)

steps.whatToRemember: רב שרביא's case survives the ברייתא's challenge in two ways: either the mother's fever kept the baby alive, or the baby cried and so was able to live.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
These words apply where he does not cry out,
phrases.notes: "These words" means the ברייתא's rule that such a baby can't survive even an hour.

phrases.english: but where he cries out,
he does live.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the challenge of Step 8, in place of the fever answer
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא says no half-born baby can survive.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only means a baby who does not cry. A crying baby can live.

steps.title: An uncircumcised man may receive sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי בנאה, rules that an ערל can be purified by הזאה. He brings support from the Jews who crossed the ירדן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי בנאה: An uncircumcised man may receive sprinkling. We found that our forefathers received sprinkling while uncircumcised, as it says: "And the people came up out of the Jordan on the tenth of the first month."
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבי יוחנן teaches that the sprinkling of פרה אדומה water works even for an ערל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think an ערל cannot be purified by הזאה until after his ברית. רבי יוחנן says it does work. His support is the generation of יהושע, who came out of the ירדן on the tenth of ניסן and were circumcised only later.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling of פרה אדומה water to purify someone from טומאת מת
We have found (introduces an example from the past)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי בְּנָאָה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Bena'a:
An uncircumcised man may receive sprinkling,
phrases.notes: This is the sprinkling of פרה אדומה water that purifies someone from טומאת מת.

phrases.english: for so we found with our forefathers
that they received sprinkling while they were uncircumcised,
as it is said:
"And the people came up out of the Jordan
on the tenth of the first month."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי בְּנָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about an ערל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An ערל may receive הזאה and be purified by it.

steps.title: Why the פסוק proves the point
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the proof. They were not circumcised on the tenth because they were tired from the journey, yet their sprinkling had to be done by then. So they were sprinkled while still uncircumcised.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the tenth they did not circumcise, because of the weakness from the journey. So when was the sprinkling done for them? Wasn't it while they were uncircumcised?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out how the פסוק shows that an ערל can receive הזאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To bring the פסח on the fourteenth, they had to be purified from טומאת מת, and the first sprinkling had to happen by the tenth. On the tenth they were too worn out from the trip to have a ברית. So they were sprinkled while they were still ערלים, and it worked.

phrases.english: On the tenth they did not circumcise,
because of the weakness of the journey.
The sprinkling, when was it done for them?!
phrases.notes: To be pure for the פסח on the fourteenth, their first sprinkling had to be done by the tenth.

phrases.english: Was it not while they were uncircumcised?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the proof from the פסוק in Step 13
steps.raayaObject: That an ערל may receive הזאה
steps.raayaSupportSource: יהושע 4:19: they arrived on the tenth, uncircumcised, and still needed sprinkling by that day.

steps.title: Maybe they never brought the פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof. Maybe they did not bring a קרבן פסח at all, so they never needed sprinkling by the tenth.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe they did not bring the פסח at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes a hole in the proof. Without a פסח, there was no reason they needed to be sprinkled by the tenth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole proof depends on their needing to be pure for the קרבן פסח. If they never brought it, they could have been sprinkled later, after their ברית. Then the story proves nothing about an ערל.

phrases.english: But perhaps they did not bring the Passover offering at all?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof of Step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof that they were sprinkled while still ערלים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If they brought no פסח, they did not need to be pure by the fourteenth, so there is no proof that they were sprinkled before their ברית.

steps.title: The פסוק says they did bring the פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the challenge. A פסוק says they brought the קרבן פסח, so the proof stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: That cannot enter your mind, for it is written: "And they made the Passover."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a פסוק showing they did bring the פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since they brought the פסח, they had to be pure by the fourteenth. That means they were sprinkled while still ערלים. רבי יוחנן's ruling is upheld.

keyTerms.meaning: It cannot enter your mind (that idea is impossible)

steps.whatToRemember: An ערל may receive הזאה. The proof is the Jews in יהושע's time: they came out of the ירדן on the tenth uncircumcised, and still brought the פסח on time.

phrases.english: It cannot enter your mind,
for it is written:
"And they made the Passover."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe they skipped the פסח, so they did not need early sprinkling.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק says they did bring the פסח, so they were sprinkled while still ערלים.

steps.title: Maybe their פסח was brought in טומאה
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא challenges the proof. Maybe the people brought a פסח הבא בטומאה, so they never needed sprinkling at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא objected: But maybe it was a פסח that is brought in a state of impurity?
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא attacks the proof from יהושע's time again. He says maybe they brought their פסח while טמא, so no sprinkling was needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof needed them to be sprinkled by the tenth so they could be טהור for the פסח. If most of the nation is טמא, the פסח can be brought in טומאה anyway. Then there is no evidence that anyone was sprinkled while uncircumcised.

keyTerms.meaning: A קרבן פסח that may be brought even while impure, when most of the people are טמא

phrases.english: Mar Zutra strongly objected to it:
But perhaps it was a Pesach that comes in impurity?
phrases.notes: When most of the nation is טמא from a dead body, they may bring the פסח anyway, so no sprinkling would be needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new attack on the proof that survived the challenge in Step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof of רבי בנאה that an ערל can receive הזאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the פסח was brought in טומאה, sprinkling was never needed, so the proof falls apart

steps.title: A ברייתא says they brought it in purity
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers with a ברייתא: they circumcised, immersed, and brought their פסח in טהרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to him: It is taught clearly in a ברייתא: They circumcised, immersed, and made their פסח offerings in purity.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers מר זוטרא with a clear source. The ברייתא says the people brought their פסח in טהרה, not in טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since they were טהור, they must have been sprinkled before the פסח. And since they were not yet circumcised by the tenth, the sprinkling happened while they were ערלים. So the proof of רבי בנאה stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is taught explicitly in a ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: The proof stands: the people in יהושע's time were sprinkled while still uncircumcised, so an ערל can receive הזאה.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to him,
It is taught explicitly:
They circumcised, immersed, and performed their Pesach offerings in purity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי, תַּנְיָא בְּהֶדְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers מר זוטרא's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Citing an explicit ברייתא that rules out the challenger's possibility
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the פסח was brought in טומאה and needed no sprinkling
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסח was brought in טהרה, so sprinkling of ערלים did take place

steps.title: Uncovering at circumcision was not given to אברהם
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that the מצוה of פריעה was not given to אברהם אבינו. He proves it from the command to יהושע to circumcise the people again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר יצחק said in the name of רב: The uncovering part of מילה was not given to אברהם אבינו, as it says: "At that time ה׳ said to יהושע: Make for yourself knives of flint..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new teaching from רב. He says אברהם was commanded only to cut off the ערלה, not to do פריעה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rest of the פסוק says to circumcise the people "again, a second time." רב reads this as: people who already had a מילה like אברהם's needed to go back and do פריעה, which was added later.

keyTerms.meaning: Uncovering the corona, folding back the thin membrane under the ערלה

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Yitzchak said that Rav said:
The uncovering of circumcision was not given
to our father Avraham,
as it says: "At that time
ה׳ said to Yehoshua:
Make for yourself knives of flint, etc."
phrases.notes: יהושע 5:2. The part left out says "and circumcise the children of Israel again, a second time"; that is where the proof is.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר רַב: לֹא נִיתְּנָה פְּרִיעַת מִילָה לְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching, connected by the same story of the circumcision in יהושע's time
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מצוה of פריעה was not part of the מילה commanded to אברהם; it was given later

steps.title: Maybe it was only those never circumcised
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב: maybe יהושע circumcised only people who had never had a מילה at all, those born in the מדבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe it means those who were not circumcised, as it is written: "For all the people who came out were circumcised, and all the people who were born..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב's proof. Maybe the פסוק is talking about people who were never circumcised, not people who needed פריעה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A later פסוק says those who left מצרים were circumcised, but those born in the מדבר were not. So the command to יהושע could simply be about them, and there is no proof about פריעה.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who were born (in the מדבר)

phrases.english: But perhaps it refers to those who were not circumcised,
as it is written: "For circumcised were
all the people who came out,
and all the people who were born, etc."
phrases.notes: יהושע 5:5. It goes on to say those born in the מדבר had not been circumcised.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof רב brought
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's reading of the פסוק in יהושע as being about פריעה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק can be explained as circumcising people who never had a מילה, so it says nothing about פריעה

steps.title: The word 'again' points to uncovering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: if it were only about uncircumcised people, why does the פסוק say ״שוב״, "again"? It must be about פריעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is the meaning of "again"? Rather, is it not about פריעה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב's proof. The word ״שוב״ shows these people already had some kind of מילה before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People who were never circumcised cannot be circumcised "again." So ״שוב״ must mean going back to people who had a מילה like אברהם's and adding פריעה.

phrases.english: If so, what is "again"?
phrases.notes: This word is from the same פסוק, יהושע 5:2: "and circumcise again."

phrases.english: Rather, is it not for uncovering?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, מַאי ״שׁוּב״? אֶלָּא לָאו לִפְרִיעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading a specific word in the פסוק that the challenge cannot explain
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק is only about people born in the מדבר who were never circumcised
steps.terutzMaskana: ״שוב״ shows a second action on people already circumcised, which is פריעה

steps.title: What does 'a second time' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word ״שנית״ teaches, since ״שוב״ already said "again."
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the meaning of "a second time"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks why the פסוק also says ״שנית״ when ״שוב״ already covered "again"; the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once ״שוב״ is used for פריעה, the word ״שנית״ looks extra. The גמרא wants to know what extra lesson it carries.

phrases.english: And what is "a second time"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the reading of ״שוב״ by asking about the extra word in the same פסוק

steps.title: ״שנית״ compares the end of a מילה to its beginning
steps.stepSummary: The word ״שנית״ teaches that an unfinished end of a מילה makes the מילה incomplete, just like not starting it at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to compare the end of מילה to the beginning of מילה: just as the beginning of מילה holds it back from counting, so too the end of מילה holds it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 22: ״שנית״, a second time, teaches that a מילה with leftover pieces must be finished, or it does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״שוב״ already taught פריעה. ״שנית״ adds that the end of the מילה is just as necessary as the start. If shreds of flesh are left behind, the person is still treated as not circumcised until they are cut.

keyTerms.meaning: to compare (to treat two things as alike)
the end of the מילה, finishing the job (removing leftover shreds)
the beginning of the מילה, the basic cut
holds back, so that without it the מצוה does not count

phrases.english: To compare the end of circumcision to the beginning of circumcision:
phrases.notes: This answers step 22's question about the word ״שנית״ (יהושע 5:2).

phrases.english: just as the beginning of circumcision holds it back (without it, it does not count) —
so too the end of circumcision holds it back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22 about the extra word ״שנית״.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״שנית״ teaches that an incomplete end of the מילה (leftover shreds) makes it not count, just like the beginning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What extra lesson does ״שנית״ teach beyond ״שוב״?

steps.title: A משנה lists the shreds that make a מילה incomplete
steps.stepSummary: A משנה shows that leftover flesh covering most of the עטרה makes the מילה not count, and such a person may not eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: These are the shreds that hold back the מילה: flesh that covers most of the עטרה. And such a person does not eat תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to show that leftover pieces at the end of a מילה really do make it incomplete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה proves the הלכה behind step 23: certain shreds mean the person still counts as an ערל. Because of this, a כהן in this state may not eat תרומה, which is the rule for one who is not circumcised.

keyTerms.meaning: shreds or leftover bits of flesh
the corona, the rim of the organ
the holy portion of produce given to a כהן
as we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna: These are the shreds
that hold back the circumcision (make it not count) —
flesh that covers [most of] the corona,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets, "most of," is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: and he does not eat teruma.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: אֵלּוּ הֵן צִיצִין הַמְעַכְּבִין אֶת הַמִּילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 23's claim that the end of a מילה is required.
steps.raayaObject: That leftover shreds at the end of a מילה make it not count.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in שבת 137a about shreds covering most of the עטרה.
steps.whatToRemember: ״שוב״ teaches פריעה, and ״שנית״ teaches that leftover shreds must be removed too. Without them, the מילה does not count.

steps.title: Most of the height of the עטרה
steps.stepSummary: רבינא (or, some say, רב ירמיה בר אבא in the name of רב) explains that "most of the עטרה" also includes flesh covering most of its height.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said, and some say רב ירמיה בר אבא said in the name of רב: it means flesh that covers most of the height of the עטרה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא (or, in another version, רב ירמיה בר אבא quoting רב) defines exactly how much leftover flesh counts as "most of the עטרה" in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think "most" means only most of the way around. This statement adds that flesh covering most of the height of the עטרה also makes the מילה incomplete. This makes the rule stricter and clearer.

keyTerms.meaning: and some say (the statement is said in another person's name)

phrases.english: Ravina said, and some say

phrases.aramaic: רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said in the name of Rav:
flesh that covers most of
the height of the corona.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the word רוב in the משנה of step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Flesh covering most of the height of the עטרה is also a shred that makes the מילה not count.

steps.title: Why no מילה in the מדבר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the story of יהושע and asks why the people did not do מילה in the מדבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in the מדבר, what is the reason they did not circumcise?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the story of יהושע and asks why the boys born in the מדבר were not circumcised. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 said some people born in the מדבר never had a מילה at all. That is strange, since the תורה had already been given. The גמרא wants to know what stopped them.

keyTerms.meaning: the wilderness, where the Jews traveled for 40 years

phrases.english: And in the wilderness, what is the reason
that they did not circumcise?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about shreds and returns to the story of יהושע's מילה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the Jews did not perform מילה during the years in the מדבר.

steps.title: First answer: too weak from traveling
steps.stepSummary: The first answer is that the hard journey left the people too weak to undergo מילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it was because of the weakness caused by the journey,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first reason: traveling in the מדבר made people too weak to do מילה safely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מילה weakens a person, and doing it while constantly traveling would be dangerous. So they held off. The words איבעית אימא signal that a second possible answer is coming next.

keyTerms.meaning: if you want, say (introduces one of several possible answers)
the weakness that comes from traveling

phrases.english: If you want, say
it was because of the weakness from the journey,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They did not do מילה because the journey made them too weak.
